title: fix(service-automation): a runtime-disabled holder's trigger binding still dispatches its flow slot (ADR-0150 D3, #33386 amendment 3)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cx5ZPCyTk8ckTsx4ut

Part of #33386 (split out of PR #33646 by seat 5's routing ruling, after review#3's PASS record 6891968637 at 4a3db01c).

## What

Amendment 3 of seat ruling 6884403301 on #33386 includes **"trigger binding: no dispatch"**: a trigger bound to a flow slot of a holder whose package is disabled should not dispatch that slot. PR #33646 implements the other run-side parts of amendment 3 (bare run doors, MCP resume) but not this one.

## Observation (review#3, 6891968637)

A **runtime-disabled** holder's trigger still fires its slot. `main` behaves the same, so #33646 does not regress it; the gap predates it.

## Acceptance

- A trigger binding (record-change, schedule, and any other trigger family that dispatches a flow slot) does not dispatch a slot whose holding package is disabled at runtime; it dispatches again after re-enable.
- Boot-disabled and runtime-disabled pinned in both registration orders of a name two packages hold, plus a one-holder CONTROL.
- Durable coordinates (slot keys, run keys, `flowDispatchHolder`) stay judged over every holder (amendment 7).
- Clause-② answer and changeset per AGENTS.md (likely `yes (narrowing)` with `!`).

Area: E2 (lease:E2). Files: `packages/services/service-automation` engine/trigger dispatch, trigger plugins (`trigger-record-change`, `trigger-schedule`).
